title: Remembrance and the Image of God
english: It is possible to fail to remember those things which were previously described as having precise and complete knowledge, following the command: 'To the end, into remembrance, to save me, Lord, you are' (Ps 69:3-4). This is the saving of everyone who has cast away the use and knowledge of the good through forgetfulness.

For all, having been made straight according to the image and likeness of God, have the thoughts concerning God scattered within them. For sin always enters through negligence; if it happens that after its practice one repents, he remembers the good, for his thought is rational and having become according to the image of God.

Since sin is led by insensitivity and ignorance of the good, and because of this one acts with pleasure and boldness, it is said concerning some that they have glory upon which they ought to be ashamed; for he says, 'The glory is in their shame' (Ps 69:3). And the prophet says, 'Be ashamed of your boasting' (Ps 69:3), for it brings mockery and destruction.

Those running toward evil without feeling, if they were to receive feeling and thought of it, would cease to desire to do it; the good turns them from the evil to do the good. He says that this very thing happens to those destined for various things: 'They would have been ashamed, knowing they are evil, having been ensnared and having failed to remember what they did; for they sought to lead my soul into the same wickedness as theirs, or to kill me, because I do not run with them into the apostasy in which they are outside of God' (Ps 51:13).

Saying this, he reproaches them, saying, 'They would have turned back, no longer desiring to hasten toward evil, and they would have been ashamed, regarding those things on which they acted wickedly, desiring that which harms me to be for me' (Ps 51:14). The one repenting turns back, running again toward what he left, desiring to be with the good and to be ashamed, even though before the repentance he spoke arrogantly against the one being persecuted, saying, 'Well done, well done,' that is, 'Let us prevail, as you flee from us' (Ps 51:15).

One must watch those who desire evil toward me; until they have the power to intend to do evil and harm, they will not be able to bring about evil, unless God delivers them (Ps 51:16). Not those who plot against money, but those who plot against the soul.
But the assault on the soul from God is alienation.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: God as Refuge and the Hope of Youth
english: Hope is held toward a person. One must strive, for the Lord holds hope; for blessed is the man who has trusted in the Lord (Ps 40:4), and he will be the Lord's hope. For this hope is living; therefore it is written, 'Born again into a living hope' (1 Pet 1:3). It has been said by the one possessing it, 'Not to be put to shame through the ages; and in your righteousness save me and bring me out' (Ps 7:10). God saves in righteousness those who hasten to be outside of iniquities, just as in wisdom He takes to Himself those who desire to possess it. And he who says the things set forth prays to be saved and to be set apart even from those who do wrong, 'Stand fast.' For it seems to follow to submit this to those spoken of in the prophecy 'For the sake of other captives' (Ps 141:7); for they do not justly demand to be saved and set apart. For some were doing wrong, but the Israelites did no wrong. It shall also be said thus: since practical virtue is named righteousness, and every sin in practice is injustice from the opposite, he who loves [God] deserves to be saved from injustice, [whereas he] who hates his own soul. And the testimony of saying thus of universal virtue, 'Walking blamelessly and working righteousness,' and the testimony of calling universal sin 'injustice,' is found in: 'I hated and detested injustice' (Ps 52:9), and 'The blood of Jesus Christ will cleanse us from all injustice' (1 John 1:7). He who wishes to surpass the shadow according to the law says this, believing in Jesus Christ, so that he might be found not having in himself his own righteousness from the law, but the righteousness of God, reckoned toward righteousness. O Lord, [not] of much superiority toward the creatures, but especially toward us humans, to cry out so much, we are not strong enough to reach your ears with the prayer which we offer up; therefore I entreat you by much goodness to incline your way of condescension toward me, so that you might save me, receiving the prayer concerning salvation. Of many desiring to fight me, become my defender; cover me with your shield, concerning which it is said, 'His truth shall surround you with a shield' (Ps 5:12). And since I want you to be for me all things, to become for me an invincible fortress and an unshakeable bulwark, most fortified.

You are a place where I remain outside of all fear from enemies, my refuge and my stronghold. Regarding Ps 70:4, the hand of a sinner is a sinful practice from which it is worthy to be rescued, so that he may not act according to it to any extent. Likewise, when one transgresses and acts wickedly, the effective energies of his actions are placed outside of him, having been rescued by God. Whether the sinner himself or another is the subject of the transgressing and acting wickedly, examine this. For it seems to incline toward the two, if a sinner who transgresses and acts wickedly exists. But if the devil is meant by these names, his hand must be seized and his military-like power must be arranged against every evil and unclean spirit. He who is rescued from the hand of those things, having become under the mighty hand of God, is snatched by nothing from it.

Just as God is the wisdom and power of the holy one, so also He is the endurance and hope of the one enduring unto salvation and hoping in Him. For it is said about these things in the 70th Psalm, 'But now where is my hope? Is it not the Lord?' (Ps 70:5) and in the 71st, 'My hope is in God, the hope of all the ends of the earth' (Ps 71:5). One must oversee 'My hope' from youth, being able to demonstrate how one, having been brought up according to God from infancy, has never possessed any hope other than God. And in addition to this, you will say that from youth there is some hope in God, from which, having stripped off the old man, you put on the new and fresh [man], created according to God in holiness and knowledge of the truth.

Regarding Ps 70:6ab, 'From the womb from my mother's belly' must be understood wisely, not meaning from the time of birth, but rather then moving logically and God-fearingly regarding the one being born; for it is written, 'Even Samuel, before knowing God' (1 Sam 3:7), although he was brought up God-fearingly from tender nails by God-fearing parents. For the children of men have a time from which they are able to move logically. The great Moses says in the wilderness, 'And all the children with us today will not enter into the land of promise, if indeed they do not enter good or evil' (Num 14:29-30). The children do not know good or evil before the fulfillment of the decisive word, how those who know God in this age [do so], just as...

title: The Remembrance in God vs. Human Glory
english: To be supported upon Him by choice?

While others are praising rulers, teachers of human lessons, and those very lessons which are indeed glorious and constitute an honorable wealth, our remembrance is in you and not in any other. A scripture is brought forward saying: 'My remembrance is in you always' (Ps 70:5). Regarding both types of scriptures, one must choose 'always' over 'throughout,' to have the remembrance and the recollection continually and without interruption in God.

Those who despise virtue and consider piety an abomination, sinners, are defiling the diligent and the lowly, calling it a terror. For they say among themselves, 'Let us give up the righteous one, since he is troublesome to us.' And since those who think and speak such things are vile to us, they say, 'It is not at all a terror, but it has happened to the many, that is, to the most vulgar,' and they flee from virtue. But even if they speak to me in that same manner, you, being stronger, protect me without harm from them. With this same thought the apostle also says that we have become a cleansing for the world and a reproach to all men (1 Cor 4:10-13). In agreement with this is also: 'We are fools for Christ, but you are wise' (1 Cor 4:10). From the same disposition is also written: 'For I think that what God has shown us the apostles to be, we are last, as if marked for execution' (1 Cor 4:13), and 'That we became a spectacle to the world' (1 Cor 4:9). Such also is what was said to the sinners by God: 'And I will be a terror to Ezekiel' (Ezek 4:14), as the prophet himself says, because of what happens most symbolically through him, to lay this one down for so many days on the right side, and so many again on the left, and the shaving of the hairs of the body. And if even these things are referred to the Savior, appearing to the many as if a terror had happened because of the cross, to visit [them]... And even the appearing as if a terror: for none of the aforementioned was such as the many supposed.

Worthy is his word, the mouth having been named, to be filled with praise (Ps 70:8). But the glory of God is the discourse concerning him, his only-begotten Son; for it is said concerning Christ, as the glory of God was to be revealed upon his appearing. For the glory of God shall be revealed, in majesty...
